newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine state auditor rejects Yacyreta dam sale.
newsitem.headline: Argentine state auditor rejects Yacyreta dam sale.

text.p: The Argentine government's plans to sell off the giant Yacyreta hydroelectric dam has ran into more trouble, with the state auditing office rejecting the planned privatization.

In a report requested by a congressional privatization commission and released late Monday, the auditing office recommended that a private firm be chosen to run the dam instead of tendering the rights to sell its energy for 30 years as the government intends.

Under the auditor's scheme, the income from the sale of the dam's electricity would be used to pay off the $8.2-billion debt run up during its construction. The administrating company would be paid an annual fee of no more than $25 million.

"It is preferable from a financial point of view to tender the management but not make any anticipated sales of energy, or to do so on as minor a scale as possible, if there is no other way of financing the completion of remaining construction," the auditing office's director Enrique Paixao told local radio Tuesday.
Only 11 of Yacyreta's planned total of 20 turbines are now functioning, and work on installing the rest has been paralyzed for two months due to lack of funds.
Paixao said that the dam would generate $18 billion from electricity sales in 30 years.

The government, which hopes to garner at least $800 million from the privatization, has already run into problems in Congress with its plans for Yacyreta. A group of northern legislators of the governing Peronist Party said they oppose the sale and top party officials acknowledge the chances of a privatization bill becoming law this year are slim.

The congressmen said they were worried that plans to allow the free export of the dam's electricity to Brazil would mean more expensive power in Argentina. They also opposed the government's proposal to condone Paraguay's part of Yacyreta's debt.
Members of the opposition Radical Party are vehemently against the sale, and protestors stormed the site in August.
Argentine congressmen opposed to the privatization met with Paraguayan counterparts in Asuncion Monday, and agreed to set up commissions to investigate the issue.

Yacyreta was constructed as a 50-50 joint-venture between the governments of Argentina and Paraguay but was entirely paid for by Argentina. Under the original agreement signed 23 years ago, Paraguay was to pay its share of the costs with electricity produced by the dam.

Yacyreta, whose first turbines began to generate power in late 1994, has always been controversial. It ran vastly over budget, was the subject of accusations of corruption, and has recently been blamed for the death of large numbers of fish in the Parana River.
